items.stem: A student is shown the relation $S$, which consists of the ordered pairs $(-3,4)$, $(1,7)$, $(2,4)$ and $(5,9)$. She says that $S$ is not a function because the number $4$ shows up twice. Which response is correct?
items.hint: Settle the two questions separately: one of them looks only at the first coordinates, the other only at the second.
worked: List the first coordinates: $-3$, $1$, $2$, $5$. They are all different, so every input has exactly one output.
That is the function test, and $S$ passes it, so $S$ is a function.
Now list the second coordinates: $4$, $7$, $4$, $9$. The output $4$ comes from both $-3$ and $2$.
A repeated output does not break the function test; it only means $S$ is not one-to-one. The student's reason is wrong.

options.text: The student is right: a relation is a function only when no output value is repeated, and $4$ is repeated.
The student is wrong: no input value is repeated, so $S$ is a one-to-one function.
The student is wrong: the inputs $-3$, $1$, $2$, $5$ are all different, so $S$ is a function; the repeated output $4$ only means $S$ is not one-to-one.
The student is wrong: $S$ is a function, and its inverse function consists of the pairs $(-3,\dfrac{1}{4})$, $(1,\dfrac{1}{7})$, $(2,\dfrac{1}{4})$ and $(5,\dfrac{1}{9})$.

items.stem: Solve $x=y^{2}+3$ for $y$, then decide whether the equation defines $y$ as a function of $x$.
items.hint: Get $y$ by itself first, then feed in one number for $x$ and count how many values of $y$ come back.
worked: Take square roots of both sides and keep both signs: $y=\pm\sqrt{x-3}$.
Test an input: at $x=7$ this gives $y^{2}=4$, so $y=2$ and $y=-2$.
One value of $x$ produces two values of $y$, so the equation does not define $y$ as a function of $x$.

options.text: $y=\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{3}$; yes, it defines $y$ as a function of $x$.
$y=\pm\sqrt{x-3}$; no, it does not define $y$ as a function of $x$, since $x=7$ gives both $y=2$ and $y=-2$.
$y=\sqrt{x-3}$; yes, it defines $y$ as a function of $x$.
$y=\pm\sqrt{x-3}$; yes, it defines $y$ as a function of $x$, because each value of $y$ produces exactly one value of $x$.

items.stem: The graph of $y=f(x)$ falls from left to right for $x<0$, reaches its lowest point at $(0,-2)$, and rises for $x>0$. Every vertical line meets this graph exactly once. Which statement is true?
items.hint: Two different tests are in play: vertical lines answer one question about $f$, horizontal lines answer a different one.
worked: Every vertical line meets the graph once, so $f$ passes the vertical line test and is a function.
The graph falls to $(0,-2)$ and then rises, so the horizontal line $y=-1$ meets it twice, once on each side of the low point.
Failing the horizontal line test means two different inputs share an output, so $f$ is not one-to-one.
A function has an inverse function only when it is one-to-one, so $f$ has none as it stands; restricting the domain to $x\ge 0$ would repair that.

options.text: $f$ is one-to-one, because every vertical line meets the graph exactly once.
Even with the domain restricted to $x\ge 0$, $f$ has no inverse function, because the graph still fails the horizontal line test.
$f$ is a function but is not one-to-one, so it has no inverse function unless its domain is restricted.
